title: Lynxight alerts lifeguards to an unconscious swimmer at Inglewood Pool; he recovers fully after rescue
summary: Lynxight, a camera system at a Perth pool, alerted a lifeguard's smartwatch to a man who had sunk unconscious; lifeguards and a swimmer rescued him, and he recovered fully.
account: The outdoor pool at Stirling Leisure - Inglewood, Perth, had used Lynxight since a redevelopment ended in September 2024, according to the City of Stirling. On 10 June 2025, a man suffered a medical episode and sank in the pool. The City of Stirling reports that the lifeguard on patrol did not see the man go under. Lynxight sent lifeguard Cameron Menzies a smartwatch alert with the swimmer's location and images. Another swimmer, Ofer Lefelman, independently noticed the emergency and lifted the man to the surface. Menzies and fellow lifeguards brought him out of the water. The City of Stirling reports that he was conscious when paramedics took him away and later recovered fully. 7NEWS reported the rescue on 1 July 2025. ABC News reported on 31 December 2025 that the system was still in use at Inglewood. In that report the city's operations coordinator credited the alert with accelerating the lifeguard's response. ABC also reported that Royal Life Saving Australia is studying the system's impact in a research partnership with Lynxight. In the same report, Paul Salmon of the University of the Sunshine Coast asked how pools will prevent over-reliance on the technology and the loss of detection skills in lifeguards.
purpose: Lynxight is built to detect swimmers in distress and to alert lifeguards. This alert was that use.

brief: On 10 June 2025, a man suffered a medical episode and sank in the outdoor pool at Stirling Leisure - Inglewood in Perth. Lynxight, a camera system built to detect swimmers in distress, sent lifeguard Cameron Menzies a smartwatch alert with the swimmer's location and images. Another swimmer, Ofer Lefelman, noticed the emergency on his own and lifted the man to the surface.[1] Menzies and fellow lifeguards brought him out of the water. The City of Stirling reports that he was conscious when paramedics took him away and that he later recovered fully.[2] Help came by two routes: The alert reached a lifeguard who had not seen the man sink, and a fellow swimmer noticed him independently.[3] The sources do not show whether he would have survived without the alert.

fields.summary: Lynxight, a camera system at a Perth pool, alerted a lifeguard's smartwatch to a man who had sunk unconscious; lifeguards and a swimmer rescued him, and he recovered fully.
fields.account: The outdoor pool at Stirling Leisure - Inglewood, Perth, had used Lynxight since a redevelopment ended in September 2024, according to the City of Stirling. On 10 June 2025, a man suffered a medical episode and sank in the pool. The City of Stirling reports that the lifeguard on patrol did not see the man go under. Lynxight sent lifeguard Cameron Menzies a smartwatch alert with the swimmer's location and images. Another swimmer, Ofer Lefelman, independently noticed the emergency and lifted the man to the surface. Menzies and fellow lifeguards brought him out of the water. The City of Stirling reports that he was conscious when paramedics took him away and later recovered fully. 7NEWS reported the rescue on 1 July 2025. ABC News reported on 31 December 2025 that the system was still in use at Inglewood. In that report the city's operations coordinator credited the alert with accelerating the lifeguard's response. ABC also reported that Royal Life Saving Australia is studying the system's impact in a research partnership with Lynxight. In the same report, Paul Salmon of the University of the Sunshine Coast asked how pools will prevent over-reliance on the technology and the loss of detection skills in lifeguards.
